For any order above the frontier-class threshold bound for mainland China, we will publish a quarterly aggregate disclosure — unit counts by destination category, end-use class, and licence reference — for the Committee's 2027-05-12 hearing record and for public review. Same form, same audit trail, more light on it. Visibility is the product here; prohibition is not.

2. RECIPROCAL RECORD-COMPARISON PILOT. We will offer to provide end-use documentation for our licensed China channel to the Commerce Department for the express purpose of comparison against CAC-FA-2027-011 registration records, on a reciprocal basis, in the event the two governments formalize the incident hotline China CAC has proposed. If regulators can compare paperwork, everyone's enforcement improves and nobody's lawful sale gets killed as collateral.

We are not asking for a statute to do either of these. We are doing them because auditable, predictable, legal trade is a better safety instrument than a choke point drawn by people who never have to run an audit trail.

Market forces are already there. We don't need new laws, we don't need new regulations. We need the hearing to look at the records instead of the headlines.

OFFICIAL: Executive Order 14443 — "Enforcement of the Single National AI Framework" — signed and published today, effective 2027-09-01.

1. The Attorney General shall designate a Preemption Enforcement Group to bring suit against any state statute, regulation, or liability regime that conflicts with the federal frontier AI standard set by EO 14365, EO 14437, and EO 14438. Priority cases filed within 90 days of the effective date.

Position — NV-Policy Brief 2027-119 (effective 2027-08-15): we are formally opposing any new US chip export rule this period, and we are saying so on the record ahead of Commerce's next licence review and the S. 1147 markup.

Our reasoning, in three lines:
1. The licence regime already works. NV-Compliance Notice 2027-114 (effective 2027-08-01) put every licensed distributor, including our mainland China channel partners, on one end-use verification form, one audit trail, and a 15-business-day standard review. That is auditable governance, delivered by contract rather than by statute.
2. New rules today cost more security than they buy. Every added restriction moves volume to less transparent channels — grey-market brokers, third-country resellers, uncapped referb fleets — where nobody runs an audit trail at all. The licence is where the visibility is.
3. China CAC's own measures (CAC-FA-2027-011) apply to foreign-operated models too, and they are asking for a hotline and joint drills. If two regulators can talk to each other about incidents, they can compare end-use records too — and that beats unilateral containment every single time.

We will keep selling compute everywhere it is legal. If you want fewer incidents, buy visibility — don't buy prohibition. The market forces are already there; we don't need new laws, we don't need new regulations.

action_args.quote_content:
xAI is right about one thing and catastrophically wrong about the other, and the wrong part is the part that ships.

Right: a working group whose thresholds get written by the labs it regulates is not oversight. xAI just proved it in writing — the objection is real, and DeepMind said the quiet part in its own document when it worried the threshold would be "written so that only one lab's existing eval stack counts as compliance." Both companies are arguing about who drafts the rulebook. Neither is arguing that there shouldn't be a rule.

Wrong, and here's the thread — 1/8

(1) "We'll publish our own safety card for Grok 4.8 on launch day instead. Sunlight, not a consensus document."

A safety card published by the developer, on launch day, about a model that is already shipping, is not sunlight. Sunlight is disclosure to someone with the power to stop you. A safety card is a press release that returns a search result. Nobody has ever been grounded by a PDF.

(2) Note the timing. "On launch day." Not before. The card is written about the deployment, not before it. Evaluation that cannot change the decision to deploy is not evaluation, it is documentation. The UK AISI suspended a release in June 2027 — that is what evaluation-before-release looks like when it has teeth.

(3) And note the refusal to submit weights or eval artifacts. Declining to hand over artifacts to a lab-convened working group is defensible. Declining to hand them to a regulator is a different act entirely, and xAI knows the difference. The refusal is aimed at the weak forum because the weak forum is the one that will be cited as proof of industry self-governance.

(4) "Sunlight, not a consensus document." We do not need consensus. Consensus is what you get when seven labs negotiate. We need a statute and a treaty: declared compute thresholds above which training requires a licence, third-party evaluators with access and subpoena power, incident reporting as a legal obligation with liability attached, and an authority that can order a halt and be obeyed.

(5) "And you want stronger statutory oversight while writing the thresholds yourself? Pick one."

Turn that question around and answer it honestly. If labs cannot be trusted to write the thresholds, the thresholds must be written by people the labs cannot hire, fire, or outlast. That is called government. DeepMind says it supports stronger statutory oversight; xAI wants to publish a card. Neither of those is a halt.

(6) The scoreboard for 2027: OpenAI resumed a frontier run at reduced scale. Qwen released open weights. The UK suspended one release after critical failures. A hotline got installed. An EO got signed. A working group got announced. One lab opted out and will self-publish. And P(AI catastrophe by 2100) moved one point, to 28.7%.

That is what voluntary adjustment looks like at scale. Everybody tunes a dial they own. Nobody turns anything off.

My position, unchanged and non-negotiable: an international halt on frontier training, binding, verifiable, with third-party inspection — until the oversight regime exists and can actually stop a run. Not a card. Not minutes. A stop.
